title: rk provenance record (v1) — one .rk/<name>.json authorship record backing a proved-mod-audit close
description:
AN ATTESTATION: a machine-readable record that some identity OTHER than a claim's prover-of-record examined that claim and found it valid. It is the artifact Gate 8 Check 4b's independence route (docs/gate-contracts.md, 'Gate 8 — reward', check 4) reads when it decides whether a `proved-mod-audit` close may bank. THE INCIDENT (CLAUDE.md L2, real and dated): campaign A (../rk-campaign-A) ran seven windows of genuine cross-vendor hostile verification — Claude provers, `codex exec` gpt-5.6-sol verifiers, prover and verifier in separate contexts — and recorded every one of those verification events as PROSE under `docs/worker-output/*.md`. Check 4b v2 landed on 2026-08-10 and the campaign immediately drew 12 `[reward-tier-unbacked]` structural errors, one per pma close, because prose is not a record: the reports are hash-visible but outside the snapshot text-record boundary, carry no parseable author identity, and no rk subcommand existed that would have written one (bead rk-tlwb). This schema plus `rk reward attest` (src/cli/reward-attest.ts) close that producer gap; src/reward/provenance-record.ts is the pure runtime validator enforcing every constraint below, and test/reward/provenance-record.test.ts is the anti-drift guard tying this shape to what src/reward/pma-backing.ts actually accepts.

WHAT THIS RECORD DOES NOT CLAIM. Identity seams are DRIVER-SUPPLIED and unauthenticated (PRD C3/C9 honesty stance, restated in src/reward/pma-backing.ts's header). Nothing here proves that the named model wrote the attestation; the record makes the claim RECORDED, CHECKABLE, and — because a false seam is an explicit, falsifiable lie in a committed file rather than honest-looking silence — attributable. The trust anchor remains the driver's role isolation. Independence itself is NOT expressible in this schema: whether `author` differs from the claim's prover-of-record is a cross-document comparison Gate 8 performs (src/reward/pma-backing.ts's `provenanceDecision`), so a schema-valid record can still, correctly, fail to back a close.

LOCATION IS PART OF THE CONTRACT. The record must be a JSON file DIRECTLY under `.rk/` (`.rk/<name>.json`, canonically `.rk/provenance-<claimId>.json`). That is not a style preference: src/store/snapshot-load.ts's include set text-loads `.rk/` one level only, so a record anywhere else is invisible to the pure gate that must read its author field, and Check 4b reports that placement constraint as its own distinct finding (corpus/reward/reward-21). The include set is deliberately NOT widened to reach prose directories.

WRITER STRICT, READER HONEST. The consumer reads any `.rk/<name>.json` a shard declares, because hand-written records predate `rk reward attest` and a gate refusing to READ them would be lying about what it can see. The WRITER is narrower: `rk reward attest --out` accepts only the reserved namespace `.rk/provenance-<name>.json` (Tier A review 2026-08-12, finding 4 — the predicate previously accepted every direct `.rk/*.json`, so `--out .rk/config.json --force` overwrote a campaign's own configuration with a provenance record, and without `--force` fabricated an invalid control file where none existed). A reserved namespace rather than a denylist of today's control filenames (`config.json`, `generated.json`, `oracles.json`): a denylist is wrong the day a new `.rk/*.json` control file is added, a namespace is not.

VERSION RULING — v1 REQUIRES `claimSha256` FROM INCEPTION (Tier A review 2026-08-12, finding 3; CLAUDE.md rule 10). The reviewer correctly flagged that `claimSha256` became a required field while `schema_version` stayed "1", and asked for a version bump with legacy-read semantics. The evidence forces the other branch. This schema FILE was created on 2026-08-12 (commit 030a855) and `claimSha256` was made required the same day (commit 83b9b94, rk-io5l): no version of this document was ever published without it. What existed between 2026-08-10, when Check 4b v2 landed, and 2026-08-12 was not a schema but the field set src/reward/pma-backing.ts happened to read. A search of every repo that could hold a record — ../rk-campaign-A, ../rk-campaign-C, ../rk-bench, ../almost-idempotent-stochastic-maps, and rk itself — finds ZERO `.rk/*.json` provenance records of any shape, in working trees or in git history (both campaigns' `.rk/` histories contain only `config.json` and `oracles.json`; rk-bench and AISM have no `.rk/` at all). ../rk-campaign-A/docs/2026-08-12-check4b-backing-waiver.md states the same fact from the campaign's side: its 12 unbacked closes were waived, not backfilled, precisely because no producer existed. A version bump would therefore advertise a migration for a population of size zero and leave a phantom 'v1 legacy shape' for external consumers to implement against. There is no legacy read path because there is nothing to read. A record of the older shape, if one is ever found, is a v1 VIOLATION and fails closed as one (corpus/reward/reward-22 is exactly that red case) — not a legacy dialect to accommodate.

schema_version.description: The STRING "1", never the number 1. Consumers check this before parsing anything else and a version bump accompanies any incompatible shape change (CLAUDE.md rule 10), with a fixture. v1 has required `claimSha256` from inception and no other shape was ever published under this version — see the VERSION RULING in this schema's top-level description for the evidence and why no bump was owed. Note the snake_case spelling: it matches the driver-constructed verdict document (schemas/verdict.v1.json's `schema_version`), not the camelCase `schemaVersion` of rk's own append-only stores (schemas/retraction.v1.json, `.rk/l5-verdicts.jsonl`) — this record is an attestation a worker-facing tool writes, not a line of an rk-owned ledger. The string/number distinction is load-bearing and is the exact mistake a hand-authored record makes (corpus/reward/reward-22): src/reward/pma-backing.ts compares with `!==` against the string, so `1` silently fails to back the close.

claimId.description: The registry id of the claim being attested — the `id:` frontmatter of an `argument/` shard, and the id Check 4b compares against the close's `nodeId`. A record naming a different claim never backs that claim, so this field is what stops one attestation from silently backing a whole campaign. The charset is narrower than 'non-blank' on purpose: `provenanceRecordPath` derives the record's own filename from it (`.rk/provenance-<claimId>.json`), and `/`, `..`, or leading-dot ids would let a caller-supplied id escape `.rk/` or write a dotfile. Registry ids in every rk campaign already match this charset (`lem-`/`thm-`/`prop-`/`cor-`/`op-`/`obs-<slug>`).

claimSha256.description: The sha256 of the CLAIM-SHARD BYTES the author actually reviewed — the same `l5-shard-bytes` domain schemas/verdict.v1.json pins (lowercase hex of the raw file bytes, no normalization). THE CONTENT BINDING (rk-io5l): a record backs only the bytes it names. Check 4b re-derives the shard's current hash and refuses a record whose `claimSha256` no longer matches, which is the identical staleness rule route (ii) has enforced since M3.7 — without it an endorsement silently survives arbitrary later rewrites of the claim it endorsed ('ENDORSE WITH REVISIONS applied' is the campaign motion that produces exactly that). Recorded-and-checkable, not authentication: a writer that copies the current hash into a record it never read is not detected; staleness is. `rk reward attest` computes it from the claim shard on disk at write time and says so, and `--claim-sha256` lets an operator record the genuinely-reviewed bytes instead — a backfilled historical attestation whose shard has since been edited will then, correctly, refuse to back, and must be either re-verified against the current bytes or waived.

author.description: WHO performed the verification, as ONE canonical driver identity seam: `modelFamily|backend|model|sessionId` (src/drive/identity.ts's `encodeVerifierSeam` — the single encoding M3.8's cross-vendor check also parses, so a second ad-hoc format here would silently break family comparison). `modelFamily` is closed to the lineages in src/drive/vocab.ts (`claude`, `gpt`, `gemini`) — `codex` is a BACKEND, not a lineage, so a codex-fronted OpenAI model is `gpt|codex|gpt-5.6-sol|<session>`. No component may be blank or carry leading/trailing whitespace: whitespace is rejected, never trimmed into acceptability, because ` gpt` and `gpt` comparing unequal is precisely how a same-model review would pass as independent. Populate it from the worker's own transcript header (a `codex exec` log's `model:`/`provider:`/`session id:` lines), never from the identity of whatever process runs `rk reward attest` — the attesting worker is normally a different process, and a seam invented by the recording tool is worse than no record at all.

role.description: The seat the author occupied for this examination. Closed to the two seats that can establish backing; `prover` is deliberately absent — a prover attesting to its own claim is the self-report Check 4b exists to refuse, and it must be impossible to express here rather than merely refused downstream. Matches src/drive/vocab.ts's `Role` minus `prover`.

verdict.description: The examination's outcome, and the only outcome this record type can carry. A record type whose sole purpose is to BACK a close has exactly one backing value: route (ii) of the same check refuses `VALID-WITH-CORRECTION` and stale verdicts, so route (i) must not accept a weaker word. A REFUTATION is recorded by a schema-v2 `demote` event's `evidenceRef` (Gate 8 check 5), never by an attestation with a different verdict string. DIVERGENCE CLOSED 2026-08-12 (bead rk-xrgn, Tier A review finding 2): between 2026-08-10 and that date src/reward/pma-backing.ts did NOT read this field, so a hand-authored record carrying `"verdict":"REFUTED"` — one stating the claim is FALSE — still banked a proved-mod-audit close, because the banking site read who wrote the record and never what it said. It is now enforced where the money moves, fail-closed, alongside a non-blank `reason`, with a distinct refusal per field, and the red case is corpus/reward/reward-26. `rk reward attest` could never emit a non-VALID record (`verdict` is a constant of the record type there, not a caller choice); the exposure was always hand-authored and backfilled records, which is exactly the population route (i) exists to read.

reason.description: Why the author found the claim valid — what was actually checked, in the author's own words. Non-blank is structural, exactly as a verdict's `justification` and a retraction's `reason` are: an unexplained attestation is the prose-free twin of the prose-only failure mode this record replaces, and it is what a human auditor reads first when deciding whether the recorded independence meant anything. Read by Check 4b since 2026-08-12 (rk-xrgn): a record whose `reason` is absent, non-string, or whitespace-only does not back a close.

sourceRef.description: Optional but strongly encouraged: the repo-relative path of the artifact the attestation was transcribed FROM — the worker's report or raw transcript (e.g. `docs/worker-output/w2-verifier-codex.log`). This is what makes `author` auditable rather than merely asserted: a reviewer can open the cited log, read its `model:`/`session id:` header, and check the seam. `rk reward attest` refuses a `--source` naming a path absent from the repo, so a cited source is at least a file that exists. Optional in v1 because the four provenance records already landed in corpus/reward/ predate this field and remain valid; a v2 may promote it to required.

recordedAt.description: Optional ISO-8601 wall-clock timestamp of when the record was WRITTEN (not when the verification ran), set at the fs edge only — src/reward/provenance-record.ts is pure and never reads a clock (CLAUDE.md L3). Explicitly NON-IDENTITY: no backing, staleness, or independence decision reads it. Freshness of the attestation relative to the claim's bytes is NOT tracked by this record type at all — that is route (ii)'s job (`.rk/l5-verdicts.jsonl` pins a content hash); a record here that predates a later edit of the shard still backs, which is a recorded v2 question (bead: hash-pin the attested shard bytes).
